questions.q: What is the Cosmos DB change feed?
options: A manually-created audit table you must build yourself
A one-time export of all data in a container
A feature that must be separately enabled and configured before any changes are tracked
An ordered, persistent log of inserts and updates made to a container's items, in the order they were committed
questions.explain: The change feed is always on and automatically captures every insert and update in commit order — no setup required to start capturing changes.

questions.q: How do classic change feed and 'all versions and deletes' mode differ?
options: They are identical — the name is the only difference
Classic mode captures deletes but not inserts
Classic captures inserts and updates only; all versions and deletes mode also captures deletes and intermediate item versions
All versions and deletes mode only works with the MongoDB API
questions.explain: Classic change feed misses deletes; the newer all-versions-and-deletes mode closes that gap for a truer CDC-style stream.

questions.q: What does the Change Feed Processor library handle on your behalf?
options: Distributing work across partition ranges and checkpointing read progress via a lease container
Automatically creating new containers when throughput runs out
Encrypting all documents at rest
Rewriting the SQL query language into JavaScript
questions.explain: The processor library manages partition distribution and tracks position through a lease container, so you don't build that coordination yourself.

questions.q: What is an Azure Functions Cosmos DB trigger?
options: A managed, serverless way to consume the change feed that fires automatically as changes arrive, without running your own processor host
A setting that disables the change feed
A stored procedure registered on a Cosmos DB container
A T-SQL trigger that fires on INSERT and UPDATE statements
questions.explain: It wraps the same change feed mechanism as a serverless function, removing the need to host a Change Feed Processor yourself.

questions.q: Which of these is a real use case for the change feed described in this lesson?
options: Replacing the need for partition keys entirely
Encrypting documents before they are written
Enforcing referential integrity between containers
Keeping a denormalized materialized view automatically in sync with a source container
questions.explain: Materialized views, event-driven architectures, and real-time analytics are the real use cases this lesson covers.
